transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I just don’t care about any of the things I used to love doing anymore—not fishing, not cooking, not even singing at church. It's like all the joy has just been drained right out of me, and I can't bring myself to do any of it.
How long have you felt this way, and was there a time before this when you had similar feelings of losing interest or joy?

It all started about a year and a half ago, shortly after my wife passed away so suddenly, and this empty feeling has been with me pretty much every day for over a year now. Before she died, I never felt anything like this at all; I was always active, working with my hands, and loved being out with people.
Have you had any period lasting at least two months during the past year and a half where you felt clearly better, with a noticeable return of your interest or ability to enjoy things?

No, I haven't had any time like that at all. This heavy, empty feeling has been almost constant, and I can only think of a few scattered days where I felt even a little bit lighter, but certainly nothing that lasted for weeks or months.
Have you ever had a period of several months where you felt completely back to your usual self before this current episode started?

No, I haven't felt back to my usual self at all since my wife passed away about a year and a half ago. Even during a brief stretch last summer when the deep sadness lifted a little bit, I was still feeling paranoid and like I was being watched, so I never truly felt normal. It's just been a constant struggle since she's been gone.

The absence of a clear two-month remission rules out F33.1, which requires distinct episodes separated by remissions. Although there is a mention of paranoia, it is not described as a prominent or persistent psychotic feature, so psychotic specifiers are not yet warranted. Thus, the current candidate is narrowed to F33.2.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent depressive episode lasting over one year without a two-month remission period, following the death of his wife. Symptoms began after a significant loss but have continued well beyond the typical bereavement period, with no return to baseline functioning, meeting criteria for recurrent depressive disorder, current episode moderate to severe without psychotic symptoms. The absence of a two-month symptom-free interval rules out adjustment disorder with prolonged depressive reaction.
